manifesto.p1: You know how to build it. You just shouldn’t have to.
manifesto.p2: Every SaaS demands the same plumbing: auth, email, an admin, translations and the tests that hold them together. Those first {headStartHours, number}+ hours are not what makes your product valuable. That work is already written and already tested. What is left is the part only you can build.

line.title: The strong foundation
line.description: Four things every SaaS needs on day one. Every one of them already runs, and every one of them is work you are not doing.

auth.title: Own your data. Protect your margins.
auth.body: Better Auth runs on your own database instead of per-user pricing that scales against you. Your user table, your sessions, your margins. The bill at 50,000 monthly actives is the same as the bill at 50, and it is zero either way.

tests.title: Know it works before you merge.
tests.body: Not vibe-coded on a weekend. {testFiles, number} test files and {e2eSpecs, plural, one {# Playwright suite} other {# Playwright suites}} run on every pull request, and the merge is blocked when a test fails or coverage drops. Deploy on a Friday and actually take the weekend.

i18n.title: Sell in {languages, number} languages without a rewrite.
i18n.body: Locale routing, translations, timezones and currency formatting are native to the codebase, not bolted on. A {languages, number}-language catalogue with {timezones, number} timezones and {currencies, number} currencies is configured before you write a line, and a parity check fails CI the moment a translation goes missing.

edge.title: Your architecture, not someone else's.
edge.body: {generation, select, available {The CLI takes what you are building as its answers and writes that, instead of handing you one opinionated shape to fight; today it writes the options you can pick in the configurator, and the others are arriving.} other {The CLI will ask what you are building and write that, instead of handing you one opinionated shape to fight; project generation arrives in a later release.}} Vite+ and TanStack Start underneath: instant HMR and strict types while you work, a runtime built for the edge once you ship.

quality.title: Quality control
quality.body: Every statement, branch, function and line of the application code is covered by unit, integration and component tests before it merges. {testFiles, number} test files, {e2eTests, plural, one {# end-to-end test} other {# end-to-end tests}} in real browsers, and a coverage gate that runs on every pull request and again in the merge queue before every merge to main.
quality.consequence: Which is what makes an agent safe to run here. It can write as fast as it likes; nothing it breaks reaches main, and you find out at the pull request instead of in production.

auth.label: Authentication
auth.body: Better Auth with email and password, OAuth, email verification, password reset, two-factor and admin user management, running on your database.

data.label: Database

billing.body: Polar checkout, customer portal and webhooks, with regional prices and upgrades for the difference. Managing products and pricing models from the admin is arriving.

A generated project’s admin console has the dashboard, users and settings. Refunds, pricing models, blog editing and the landing page editor are arriving.

tooling.label: Tooling

compare.close: A template gets you a folder. This gets you a codebase with the tests already green, the types already strict and every vendor decision already made in your favour. One payment, with no subscription or per-user fees after it.

notFor.title: Who this is not for
notFor.body: If you want something free to learn on, clone a template and enjoy it. If you want someone else to run your auth and bill you per user for the privilege, buy that instead. This is for people who intend to own the codebase, read all of it, and still be running it in three years.

pricing.title: Buy it once
pricing.description: One payment, lifetime core updates, no per-user fees. The same economics this codebase is built to give your own customers.

ledger.lead: You are not buying code. You are buying back the calendar.
ledger.body: Price it in your own hours. At {hourlyRate} an hour, <price></price> is under {coreHours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}} of your time. The work it replaces takes far longer. It is auth with two-factor and OAuth, a typed data layer, transactional email, an admin console, a {languages, number}-language i18n layer and a test suite that actually gates the merge. Every one of those is a solved problem you would solve again, and not one of them is the reason anybody will pay you.

faq.lead: The questions buyers actually ask, answered in full. If yours is not here, send it over.
faq.contact: Ask the engineer who built it

q1.question: What exactly do I get?
q1.answer: A licence to the proprietary SaaSy Land CLI and the key that activates it. {generation, select, available {The CLI activates, shows and frees the machines your key runs on, and {initCommand} writes a SaaS application with TanStack Start, React, Vite+, Better Auth, Drizzle with Cloudflare D1, Resend and use-intl, as editable source with its tests and documentation, from the options you can pick in the configurator; billing and the other options are arriving.} other {Today the CLI activates, shows and frees the machines your key runs on. Project generation arrives in a later release: it will write a SaaS application with TanStack Start, React, Vite+, Better Auth, Drizzle with Cloudflare D1, Resend and use-intl, as editable source with its tests and documentation, starting with the options you can pick in the configurator; billing and the other options are arriving.}} Each tier’s card lists what is available now and what is arriving; Agency also covers client projects.

q2.question: Why Better Auth instead of Clerk or Auth0?
q2.answer: Ownership. Hosted auth charges you per monthly active user, which means your costs scale exactly when your revenue should. Better Auth lives in your codebase and your database. Your users are rows you own, not line items on someone else's invoice.

q3.question: Is it really {coverageThreshold, number}% code coverage?
q3.answer: Yes, for the application code: statements, branches, functions and lines, measured from the unit, integration and component tests under Vitest and enforced as a CI gate on every pull request, not reported as a screenshot. {e2eTests, plural, one {The # end-to-end test in real Chromium and WebKit does not count} other {The # end-to-end tests in real Chromium and WebKit do not count}} toward that number: the docs report them on their own, with every user and admin flow and the test that proves it or what is still missing. Both come from this public website repository.

q4.question: How do I know it is what this page says it is?
q4.answer: Read the public documentation and the repository before you buy. If you change your mind, you get a full refund within {days} days, as long as you have not generated a project or opened a paid lesson; the Refunds page explains the process. Mandatory cancellation rights and remedies for faulty or undelivered content remain protected.

q5.question: Why not just have an AI agent build this?
q5.answer: It will, and the result will look right. What it will not tell you is which of the auth edge cases it skipped, which webhook is not idempotent, or that the i18n parity check it never wrote would have caught the missing key. Generated code is the cheap part now. The expensive part is the gate that proves it is correct, and that is what this repository is: point an agent at it and it inherits {testFiles, number} test files, strict types and a CI gate that fails when it is wrong.

q6.question: Do I need the Complete tier?
q6.answer: Core gives you the machine. Complete adds the support and the reasoning around it: priority replies within {supportResponseDays, plural, =1 {one business day} other {# business days}} now; free lifetime access to {reactprojects} {reactprojectsAccess, select, available {now} other {once it opens}} and to {angularprojects} {angularprojectsAccess, select, available {now} other {once it opens}}; and the full video course from empty folder to production and a walkthrough of every module as they arrive.

q7.question: Is any of this a subscription?
q7.answer: No. You pay once. Lifetime core updates are included, the code sits in your repository, and there is no per-seat price, no monthly active user meter and no renewal date. {teamSeatsAccess, select, available {The only seats are the team seats for the course, {reactprojects} and {angularprojects} that come with Agency.} other {The only seats will be the team seats for the course, {reactprojects} and {angularprojects} that come with Agency, which are arriving.}} Each tier's card shows how many machines its key activates on at a time. A CI repository counts as one machine, and a slot you free on your licence page can be used again.

q8.question: What does “lifetime updates” cover?
q8.answer: Every release of the CLI and of the code it generates, including framework upgrades and security patches, for as long as SaaSy Land exists. Bringing an existing project up to a newer release with one command is arriving. You buy once and the machine keeps getting better.

q9.question: Can I use it for client work?
q9.answer: Core and Complete cover unlimited generated applications for your own products; Agency also covers client projects. The private CLI requires a purchase and valid key and cannot be modified or redistributed, subject to mandatory legal exceptions. You may edit and deploy generated applications. This public website and previous MIT releases remain MIT licensed.

q10.question: Why trust a starter kit built by one engineer?
q10.answer: Because the claims are checkable. The coverage report is generated by the repository, the CI workflow that enforces it is in the repository, and the person who wrote it builds production software for a living. Read the documentation before you pay and hold this page to it.

q11.question: Do I need to know Vite+ and TanStack Start?
q11.answer: No. If you know React and TypeScript, you can read the code from day one. TanStack Start handles routing and server functions, Vite+ provides the development tools, and the application runs on Cloudflare Workers. The video course, which is arriving, will cover the whole flow step by step.
